catalog.notes: Moves happen at a gaming-day boundary to an empty or swapped slot.

calibration.method: Per-zone 90th-percentile absolute residual order statistic; pooled fallback below 100 rows.

groupedCheck.method: Stable SHA-256 20% machine-ID holdout. Exclude these IDs from all inner model-selection folds and fitting; select independently, fit through April 15, then score held-out machines in May–June using origin-known metadata.

limitations: Predictive associations, not causal relocation effects. Only four observed moves, three across zones, support the entire six-month history.
May–June has already been examined during dashboard development. This is a retrospective time holdout, not an untouched prospective test.
Evaluation freezes machine metadata at each prediction origin. Machines first installed after that origin are excluded and counted; later moves do not feed future location metadata into predictions.
Expected-win rates predict wager demand at configured hold, not realized payout luck or guaranteed profit. Actual future availability, occupancy, coin-in, traffic and repairs are not features.

July points refit the selected specification on January–June. April calibration residual widths are reused only as empirical sensitivity ranges; they are not calibrated July-mean intervals or confidence intervals for relocation uplift.
Repeated machine-days and common daily shocks are dependent; nominal residual-band coverage has no formal exchangeability guarantee. Extrapolation to unsupported configuration-zone cells is blocked.
The model distinguishes zones, not individual slots within a zone. Seat inventory constrains feasibility; it does not establish slot-specific causal advantages.
Net floor benefit also depends on displaced play, both legs of swaps, costs, lead time and downtime. A prospective controlled pilot is required to test incremental benefit.

evidence.title: Time-validated placement demand scenarios
evidence.source: prepared_daily_view + dated placements + floor_locations + action_catalog; src/placement_model.py
evidence.method: Three expanding-origin inner folds select among config-weekday baseline, ridge and histogram boosting; separate April calibration; retrospective May–June score with frozen-origin metadata.
evidence.result: Selected Histogram gradient boosting; May–June weighted rate MAE $3.691 versus $4.286 baseline (13.9% difference); nominal 90% daily-rate band coverage 88.5%.
evidence.alternative: Location associations may reflect game allocation, guest mix, access and displaced play; machine-day prediction does not identify intervention uplift.
evidence.limitation: Predictive associations, not causal relocation effects. Only four observed moves, three across zones, support the entire six-month history. May–June has already been examined during dashboard development. This is a retrospective time holdout, not an untouched prospective test. July points refit the selected specification on January–June. April calibration residual widths are reused only as empirical sensitivity ranges; they are not calibrated July-mean intervals or confidence intervals for relocation uplift.
